# MIDNIGHT_KB

Midnight Network documentation, distilled into one structured knowledge base.

`SEC.01 // WHAT IS MIDNIGHT`

## Overview

Midnight is a blockchain platform for building privacy-preserving DApps. Per the docs: it "enables developers to define how data is isolated, verified, and shared through zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs and programmable confidentiality controls." It is a proof-of-stake, Substrate-based chain and the first **partner chain** to Cardano, with a native Cardano bridge. Smart contracts are written in **Compact**, a TypeScript-like DSL; each contract call is proven with a zk-SNARK — compact proofs (~128 bytes) verified in milliseconds regardless of computation complexity.

### Defining properties

- **Dual state** — public state on-chain; private state stays encrypted on the user's machine, accessed only through witness functions.
- **Dual ledger** — shielded (private) and unshielded (public) tokens coexist; assets can transition between the two.
- **Rational privacy** — shielding is opt-in; viewing keys grant read-only access to shielded transactions for compliance.
- **Local proving** — a local proof server generates all ZK proofs, so private data never leaves the user's machine.
- **Dual-component tokenomics** — NIGHT (transferable utility token) generates DUST (non-transferable fee resource), decoupling validator rewards from fee volatility.
Key papers cited by the docs: Kachina (eprint 2020/543) · Zswap (eprint 2022/1002, PoPETs 2022) · Zerocash (IEEE S&P 2014) · PoS Sidechains (eprint 2018/1239). Whitepapers: Nightpaper + Tokenomics Incentives at midnight.network/whitepaper.

`SEC.02 // SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE`

## Architecture

### 2.1 DApp stack

Every Midnight DApp assembles six providers (`MidnightProviders`). Proofs are generated locally; public state flows back through the indexer.

_FIG.A — DAPP RUNTIME TOPOLOGY_
[FIGURE] DApp runtime topology: six midnight-js providers connect to local services — proof server, encrypted private state, ZK artifacts, Lace wallet — and across the network boundary to the indexer and node. Private data and witness values never leave the machine.

### 2.2 Compile pipeline

_FIG.B — COMPACT COMPILATION_
[FIGURE] Compilation pipeline: a .compact source file goes through compactc and produces three artifacts — the TypeScript contract API, one ZKIR file per circuit, and prover plus verifier keys per circuit.

### 2.3 Transaction anatomy

A transaction contains a **guaranteed** Zswap offer, an optional **fallible** Zswap offer, an optional contract-calls segment, and binding randomness. Fees are collected in the guaranteed phase; a fallible-phase failure keeps guaranteed effects and forfeits fees. Integrity comes from homomorphically summed Pedersen commitments plus a Fiat–Shamir Schnorr proof.

_FIG.C — TRANSACTION STRUCTURE & FAILURE SEMANTICS_
[FIGURE] A transaction contains a guaranteed Zswap offer where fees are collected, an optional fallible offer, and a contract-calls segment, bound together by Pedersen commitments and binding randomness. Guaranteed-phase failure excludes the whole transaction; fallible-phase failure keeps guaranteed effects and forfeits fees.

### 2.4 Cardano partner-chain stack

_FIG.D — PARTNER-CHAIN DEPENDENCY CHAIN_
[FIGURE] Dependency chain: Cardano blockchain to Cardano node 11.0.1 to db-sync 13.7.1.0 to PostgreSQL 17 to the Midnight node. Cardano SPOs delegate stake to Midnight's permissioned validators; the cNIGHT observation pallet mirrors Cardano events into DUST supply one to one.

### 2.5 Contract execution model

Three execution environments: **ledger** (public, on-chain), **circuit** (proof logic), **witness** (private, off-chain). A call produces a public transcript plus a ZK proof that the transcript is correct; the on-chain verifier key checks it.

_FIG.E — ZK PROOF PIPELINE: CIRCUIT CALL → VERIFIED STATE CHANGE_
[FIGURE] ZK proof pipeline: private state feeds witness functions, whose untrusted outputs enter the Compact circuit; the prover turns constraints and witness assignments into a roughly 128-byte proof. Only the public transcript and the proof cross the privacy boundary; the on-chain verifier key applies effects if valid and rejects otherwise. Witness data never crosses.

`SEC.03 // HOW MIDNIGHT WORKS`

## Core Concepts

### Kachina

Kachina is "a data-protecting smart contract model that enables confidential, general-purpose smart contract functionality without sacrificing decentralization." Contracts are reactive state machines with public state (blockchain) and private state (user machine), connected by ZK proofs that private state changes justify public state changes.

### Zswap

Zswap is "a shielded token mechanism, based on Zerocash, extended with native token support and atomic swaps" (combining Zcash and SwapCT). An **offer** = inputs (spends) + outputs + transient coins (created and spent in the same tx) + a balance vector over all token types. Outputs create **commitments** in a global Merkle tree; inputs reveal unlinkable **nullifiers** that prevent double-spends. A token type is a 256-bit hash derived from contract address + domain separator (zero = native token). Two transactions can merge into an atomic swap when at least one has no contract calls.

_FIG.G — ZSWAP: COMMITMENT / NULLIFIER MECHANISM_
[FIGURE] Zswap coin lifecycle: creating a coin appends a commitment to the global Merkle tree; spending it reveals a nullifier into the nullifier set. The two records cannot be linked. A spend is valid only if the proof verifies, the Merkle root is a known past root, and the nullifier is not already in the set — otherwise it is rejected as a double spend.

### Impact VM

Impact is "a stack-based, non-Turing-complete state manipulation language." Users cannot write Impact manually; it is still under active revision. State values (immutable to the program): null, cell, Map, Array(n) with 0<n<16, MerkleTree(d) with 1≤d≤32. Values use **Field-Aligned Binary (FAB)** encoding so they can re-encode as field elements in any prime field. A transcript binds gas bound + declared effects + program; declared effects are verified against actual execution.

### Privacy patterns

The commitment/nullifier pattern acts as a single-use authentication token: commit a value into a MerkleTree publicly ("some value is in the tree, without revealing which"), then spend it once by publishing its nullifier into a Set. `persistentHash`/`persistentCommit` put private data on the public ledger without revealing content; `HistoricMerkleTree` accepts proofs against prior tree versions.

### Ledger state

Ledger state = Zswap state (coin-commitment Merkle tree, first-free index, nullifier set, valid historical roots) + a contract state map from address to Impact state value plus an entry-point→operation map, where each operation stores a SNARK verifier key. Contract deployment "creates a new contract if it does not already exist and fails otherwise"; the address is a hash of the deploy part.

### Consensus & node internals

**AURA** (proof-of-authority, round-robin slots) produces blocks every 6 s; **GRANDPA** provides asynchronous provable finality (~18 s). Cardano SPOs delegate stake to Midnight's permissioned validators. Runtime logic compiles to WASM (the state transition function); `pallet-midnight` processes proof-validated, unsigned ledger transactions; canonical state lives in a Patricia-Merkle trie persisted by ParityDB. Crypto: Blake2-256 (hashes), Sr25519 (AURA), Ed25519 (GRANDPA + libp2p), ECDSA (partner-chain messages). P2P: libp2p with Kademlia DHT, Noise encryption, Yamux multiplexing, port 30333.

### Current limits

- Cross-contract calls within circuits are not yet supported ("cross-contract calls are not yet supported" — compiler error).
- DApps requiring oracles (e.g. price feeds) cannot be built yet.
- Solidity cannot be reused — TypeScript + Compact only.
- "The details of Midnight's native currency implementation are not yet stable."
`SEC.04 // DUAL-COMPONENT TOKENOMICS`

## Token Model

Docs analogy: "NIGHT: Analogous to a Solar Panel… DUST: Analogous to Electricity."

| Aspect | NIGHT | DUST |
|---|---|---|
| Definition | "The unshielded utility token used for staking, securing the network, and governance." Transferable, persistent. | "A shielded, non-transferable resource that the network consumes to pay transaction fees." Explicitly not a token. |
| Atomic unit | Star — 1 NIGHT = 106 Stars | Speck — 1 DUST = 1015 Specks |
| Variants | cNIGHT (on Cardano) · mNIGHT (future native) · tNIGHT (testnet faucet) | tDUST (testnet) · generated, never bought |
| Role | Validator rewards stay predictable — decoupled from fee volume. | Every transaction consumes DUST; equilibrium via burn-and-mint cycles. |

### DUST generation

A DUST UTXO is created iff a NIGHT UTXO is created and the owner has a **Registration Table** entry linking NIGHT public key → DUST public key. Value is lazily evaluated at spend-time. Initial parameters: cap **5 DUST per NIGHT** (ratio 5,000,000,000); generation/decay rate 8,267 ≈ **1 week to cap**; grace period **3 hours**. Spending is a 1-to-1 self-transfer: one input UTXO (nullifier) → one output UTXO worth value − gas.

_FIG.F — DUST LIFECYCLE · VALUE OVER TIME_
[FIGURE] DUST value over time: it generates toward a cap of 5 DUST per NIGHT over about one week, holds constant at the cap, starts decaying the moment the backing NIGHT UTXO is spent — even mid-generation — and then stays at zero.

Cross-chain timing: cNIGHT registration finalizes on Cardano then reaches a Midnight node in ~12 hours; local networks generate DUST in ~5 minutes. The **Native Token Observation Pallet** watches cNIGHT events on Cardano and updates DUST supply 1:1.

### Shielded vs unshielded tokens

Four quadrants: {shielded, unshielded} × {ledger tokens (protocol-managed UTXOs, e.g. NIGHT), contract tokens (account-style, ERC-20-like, managed in Compact)}. Unshielded token balances are chain-resident and publicly readable via `unshieldedBalance(color)`. A shielded token "has no public balance to read, its value lives in immutable coins" — the chain tracks only commitments and nullifiers; partial transfers create change coins via deterministic nonce evolution (`evolveNonce()`). Token standards discussion: Midnight Improvement Proposals #142.

`SEC.05 // LANGUAGE 0.23.0 · COMPILER 0.31.x`

## Compact Language

### Contract anatomy

```
pragma language_version 0.23;
import CompactStandardLibrary;

export enum State { VACANT, OCCUPIED }
export sealed ledger authority: Bytes; // sealed: constructor-only writes
ledger round: Counter;
witness secretKey(): Bytes; // implemented in TypeScript

constructor(pk: Bytes) { authority = disclose(pk); }

export circuit act(): [] { // export circuit = entry point
 const pk = publicKey(round as Bytes, secretKey());
 assert(disclose(pk) == authority, "not authorized");
 round.increment(1);
}
circuit publicKey(r: Bytes, sk: Bytes): Bytes {
 return persistentHash>>(
 [pad(32, "midnight:examples:lock:pk"), r, sk]);
}
```
- **circuit** — compiled to a ZK circuit; no recursion, bounded loops, fixed-size types. `pure circuit` = no ledger/witness/impure calls.
- **witness** — declared in Compact, implemented in TypeScript; results are untrusted input, verify in-circuit.
- **disclose()** — compile-time annotation authorizing witness-derived data to cross visibility boundaries (ledger writes, exported returns, cross-contract). No runtime effect. The checker ("witness protection program") is an abstract interpreter tracking data flow; `transientCommit` output is exempt, `transientHash` output is not.
- **sealed ledger** — field writable only from the constructor.
_FIG.H — disclose(): THE ONLY GATE ACROSS THE VISIBILITY BOUNDARY_
[FIGURE] The disclose gate: a witness value enters the circuit as untrusted input. It may reach the public ledger only through an explicit disclose() call, which compiles; any path without disclose is rejected at compile time with the witness-value disclosure error.

### Type system

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Boolean` | true / false |
| `Field` | Unsigned integer up to the proving system's prime field order |
| `Uint` / `Uint` | Sized (≤ n bits) / bounded unsigned integer; subtyping into wider Uint and Field |
| `Bytes` | Fixed-length byte vector |
| `Opaque` · `Opaque` | Foreign JS data, opaque inside Compact only — on-chain representation is NOT hidden |
| `Vector` · `[T1, …, Tn]` | Homogeneous / heterogeneous fixed-length tuples; `[]` is unit |
| `struct` · `enum` · `type` · `new type` | Structs, enums, structural alias, nominal alias; generics via `T` and numeric `#N` |

### Ledger ADTs

| ADT | Key operations |
|---|---|
| `Cell` | `read · write · writeCoin · resetToDefault` — plain `T` is implicitly a Cell |
| `Counter` | `increment · decrement · read · lessThan`; supports `+=` |
| `Set` | `insert · insertCoin · remove · member · isEmpty · size` |
| `Map` | `insert · insertDefault · lookup · member · remove · size` — V may itself be a ledger ADT (only nesting allowed) |
| `List` | `pushFront · popFront · head → Maybe · length` |
| `MerkleTree` | `insert · insertIndex · insertHash · checkRoot · isFull` (2 ≤ n ≤ 32); TS-only: `root · firstFree · findPathForLeaf · pathForLeaf` |
| `HistoricMerkleTree` | All MerkleTree ops; `checkRoot` accepts past roots; `resetHistory` |
| `Kernel` | Chain-level ops: `balance · blockTimeGreaterThan/LessThan · claim* · mintShielded/Unshielded · self · checkpoint` |

### Standard library highlights

- Structs: `Maybe`, `Either`, `ShieldedCoinInfo` {nonce, color, value}, `QualifiedShieldedCoinInfo` (+ mtIndex), `ContractAddress`, `ZswapCoinPublicKey`, `UserAddress`, `MerkleTreeDigest/Path/PathEntry`.
- Hashing: `persistentHash / persistentCommit` (SHA-256, upgrade-stable — for long-lived state) vs `transientHash / transientCommit` (circuit-efficient, not upgrade-stable); `degradeToTransient / upgradeFromTransient` convert.
- EC ops on the native curve: `ecAdd · ecMul · ecMulGenerator · hashToCurve` (JubjubPoint since compiler 0.30.0 — formerly NativePoint).
- Tokens: `nativeToken() · tokenType(domainSep, contract) · mintShieldedToken · mintUnshieldedToken · sendShielded / sendImmediateShielded / receiveShielded · sendUnshielded / receiveUnshielded · evolveNonce · ownPublicKey()` — the docs warn: **never use `ownPublicKey()` for caller authentication**.
- Queries: `unshieldedBalance(color)` + Lt/Lte/Gt/Gte variants; `blockTimeLt/Lte/Gt/Gte` (Unix 秒).

### Security patterns

```
// Canonical nullifier pattern (from docs, verbatim)
export ledger usedNullifiers: Set>;
circuit nullifier(secretKey: Bytes): Bytes {
 return persistentHash>>([pad(32, "nullifier-domain"), secretKey]);
}
export circuit spend(secretKey: Bytes): [] {
 const nul = nullifier(secretKey);
 assert(!usedNullifiers.member(nul), "Already spent");
 usedNullifiers.insert(disclose(nul));
}
```
- Privacy by default; place `disclose()` as close to the disclosure point as possible.
- Never trust witness outputs — verify cryptographically in-circuit.
- Domain-separate every hash (`pad(32, "nullifier-domain")` vs `"commitment-domain"`); never reuse commitment salts.
- Generic error messages — no private data in asserts.

### Toolchain

| Tool | Usage |
|---|---|
| `compact` CLI | Toolchain manager: `check · update [version] · compile [+ver] src target · format [--check] · fixup [--update-Uint-ranges] · list · clean · self update`. Installer: `curl … compact-installer.sh | sh` |
| `compactc` | Compiler. Output: `contract/index.js+.d.ts`, `zkir/*.zkir`, `keys/*.prover|.verifier`. Flags: `--skip-zk · --language-version · --ledger-version · --compact-path · --vscode` |
| Proof server | `docker run -d -p 6300:6300 midnightntwrk/proof-server:8.1.0 -- midnight-proof-server --network preprod` — port 6300 "should not be changed" |
| Editors | VS Code extension 0.2.13 (.vsix, official) · Neovim community plugin `1NickPappas/compact.vim` (no LSP) |
| Lint / test | `npx compact-zkir-lint -r managed/*/zkir` · Jest/Vitest against generated `Contract` class (`contract.impureCircuits.name(context, …)`) |

Contract updatability: default deploy = empty maintenance committee, threshold 1 → permanently immutable (may break on proof-system upgrades). Alternative: a **contract maintenance authority** can replace verifier keys/circuits (`circuitMaintenanceTx.*.insertVerifierKey`, `contractMaintenanceTx.replaceAuthority`).

`SEC.06 // BUILD → PROVE → DEPLOY`

## Developer Workflow

Canonical loop: write Compact → `compact compile` → implement TypeScript witnesses → wrap generated bindings in an API class → assemble six providers → `deployContract` / `findDeployedContract` → circuit calls prove via the local proof server → wallet balances & signs (adds DUST fees + Zswap proofs) → node → indexer streams state back as RxJS observables.

### Quick start

```
# Toolchain
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf \
 https://github.com/midnightntwrk/compact/releases/latest/download/compact-installer.sh | sh
compact update

# Scaffold + local devnet (node + indexer + proof server, pre-minted NIGHT)
npx create-mn-app # templates: hello-world, battleship, bboard, leaderboard
npm run setup # boots devnet, compiles, deploys
npm run network preview # switch: undeployed | preview | preprod
```

`SEC.08 // INFRASTRUCTURE`

## Node Operations

| Node type | Role |
|---|---|
| Full node | "Validates transactions and maintains current blockchain state"; prunes history (default retention 256 blocks) |
| Archive node | Complete history, `--pruning archive` |
| Boot node | "Initial connection points for nodes joining the Midnight Network" — peer discovery, voluntary |
| RPC node | "The primary interface for applications" — HTTP/WS :9944, `--rpc-methods Safe`, front with nginx/Caddy for TLS + rate limits |

Dependency chain: Cardano node v11.0.1 (Mithril snapshot bootstrap ≈ 20 min) → cardano-db-sync 13.7.1.0 → PostgreSQL 17 → midnight-node. Consensus AURA/GRANDPA, permissioned validators, 6 s blocks. P2P port 30333. Chain flag: `--chain local|preview|preprod|mainnet`. Guides are Linux x86-64, binary + systemd (no Docker for nodes). Mainnet host: 32 GB+ RAM, 4+ cores, 320 GB NVMe, 60k IOPS, GLIBC 2.39+; testnet halves most of that.

Transaction rejections surface as Substrate `InvalidTransaction::Custom(u8)` — see SEC.10 for the 1010 error decode table. No SPO key-registration steps are published in the /nodes section (block production is permissioned).

`SEC.10 // PROBLEM → CAUSE → FIX`

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause → Fix |
|---|---|
| "potential witness-value disclosure must be declared" | Witness data flowing to ledger/exported return without authorization → wrap in `disclose()` |
| "version mismatch: compiled code expects X, runtime is Y" | compact-runtime ↔ compiler drift → align versions per matrix or recompile |
| Substrate 1010 "Invalid Transaction" | Decode inner `Custom error: N`: 0–11 deserialization · 100–109 invalid (108 replay counter) · 110–139 malformed (115 bad ZK proof) · 150–157 infra (154 block limit, 155 fee calc → refresh estimate) · 166 network-ID mismatch |
| npm 403 on @midnight-ntwrk/* | Wrong registry / VPN / stale scope config → `npm config set registry https://registry.npmjs.org/`, delete scope override, clean cache |
| `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT` | Stale terminal/Node — need Node 22+ (`nvm use`), `rm -rf node_modules/.cache` |
| Wallet sync crash on Node v20 | Iterator helpers missing → Node 22+ required |
| compactc "No such file or directory" on NixOS | Non-FHS shebang → buildFHSEnv shell + patch shebang to `#!/usr/bin/env bash` |
| Proof generation fails / slow | Check circuit complexity, bounded loops, witness sizes, memory; keep proof-server terminal open during compilation |
| Exit codes (compactc) | 0 success · 1 bad CLI args · 255 compilation failed |

Support: Discord #support (accept #rules first) · support@midnight.network. Security vulnerabilities: email only, never Discord; public disclosure after fix.

`SEC.11 // TERMINOLOGY — AS DEFINED BY THE DOCS`

## Glossary

Terms preserved exactly as the docs define them (official /glossary page + canonical definitions from concept pages, deduplicated). EN definition first, ZH translation follows.

### Platform & protocol

- **Kachina** — "A unified security model for data-protecting smart contracts that bridge the gap between private state on the user's local machine and public state on the blockchain."
- **Zswap** — "A transaction scheme that combines the strengths of Zcash and SwapCT" — shielded multi-asset tokens with atomic swaps.
- **Impact** — Stack-based, non-Turing-complete on-chain state manipulation language (the VM); not hand-writable.
- **Partner chain** — A chain inheriting security from an established layer; Midnight is the first partner chain to Cardano.
- **Firewall property** — "The failure of one ledger must not endanger the security of other connected ledgers."
- **AURA / GRANDPA** — PoA round-robin block production / asynchronous provable finality gadget.
- **pallet-midnight** — "The core pallet powering Midnight's privacy-preserving transaction logic."
- **Runtime upgrade** — Evolving a Substrate chain by storing the state-transition code on-chain and updating it via dedicated transactions.
- **Guaranteed / fallible phase** — Two-phase execution: guaranteed must succeed for inclusion (fees collected here); fallible failure keeps guaranteed effects.
- **Transcript** — The declared record of a call's visible effects — gas bound + effects + program; verified against actual execution.
- **System transaction** — Governance-gated, root-origin state change; not user-submittable.
- **Universally Composable (UC)** — "A theoretical framework used to analyze and prove the security of cryptographic protocols in a composable manner."
- **Zero-knowledge proof (ZKP)** — "Allows someone to prove they know a secret without revealing the secret."
- **ZK-SNARK** — Succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge; ~128-byte proofs, millisecond verification, size independent of computation.
- **ZK circuit** — "Arithmetic circuits are short programs consisting of a fixed number of multiplications and additions in a modular prime field."
- **Witness (logic)** — "In mathematical logic, a witness is a value that satisfies an assertion" — in Midnight: the prover's private input.
- **Commitment** — "Allows a party to commit to a chosen value while keeping it hidden" — binding and hiding.
- **Nullifier** — "A unique value derived from a coin or private state element that is revealed on-chain when that element is consumed" — prevents double-spends, unlinkably.
- **Pedersen commitment** — Homomorphic commitment scheme (Pedersen, 1992); summed across a transaction for balance integrity.
- **Blinding factor** — "A random value used in cryptographic commitment schemes … to hide the underlying data."
- **Proving / verification key** — Per-circuit artifacts from the SNARK setup: large prover key generates proofs; compact verifier key checks them on-chain.
- **Halo 2** — "A high-performance ZK Snark implementation from the Electric Coin company."
- **Midnight SRS** — Structured Reference String introduced in Ledger 7.0.0 — invalidated all prior proofs and verifier keys.
- **Jubjub curve** — "Midnight's native internal curve" — in-circuit EC ops and Schnorr signatures (JubjubPoint).
- **Selective disclosure** — "Allows a user to reveal only a specific subset of their personal data or attributes to a verifier."
- **Viewing key** — Read-only access to shielded transactions (compliance); also the indexer session credential.
- **NIGHT** — "Midnight's native utility token, transferable and persistent, used for governance, incentives, and as the source of DUST generation."
- **DUST** — "A shielded, non-transferable, consumable network resource used exclusively to pay transaction fees on Midnight."
- **STAR / SPECK** — Atomic units: 1 NIGHT = 10⁶ STAR; 1 DUST = 10¹⁵ SPECK.
- **cNIGHT / mNIGHT / tNIGHT / tDUST** — NIGHT on Cardano / future native NIGHT on Midnight / testnet NIGHT / testnet DUST (no real-world value).
- **Registration Table** — On-chain mapping NIGHT public key → DUST public key; prerequisite for DUST generation.
- **Shielded / Unshielded** — Shielded: "interactions occur without metadata leakage." Unshielded: addresses and amounts visible on the public ledger.
- **Ledger / Contract tokens** — Protocol-managed UTXOs on-chain vs account-style tokens managed inside Compact contracts (ERC-20-like).
- **Token type / color** — 256-bit hash derived from contract address + domain separator; zero = native token.
- **Qualified coin** — "A coin registered in the ledger's commitment Merkle tree with a known index and so qualified to be spent."
- **Transient coin** — "Coins that are both created and spent in the same transaction."
- **Transaction balancing** — "If a wallet receives a transaction that is not balanced, the wallet balances [it] by providing necessary inputs and outputs" (+ DUST fees).
- **UTXO** — Unspent Transaction Output — a discrete digital coin; Midnight marks spends via a nullifier set.
- **Blockchain space tokenization** — Tokenized transaction capacity — pay in advance for regular inclusion.
- **Compact** — "The domain-specific language, based on TypeScript, in which Midnight's smart contracts are expressed."
- **Circuit (Compact)** — Exported Compact function compiled to ZK proof logic; proven locally, verified on-chain without revealing private inputs.
- **Witness (Compact)** — Function declared in Compact, implemented in TypeScript; supplies private data at proving time; untrusted.
- **disclose()** — Compiler directive marking witness-derived values as intentionally safe to expose; no runtime effect.
- **Private oracle** — "The set of witness functions and the private state over which they operate constitute the private oracle for a contract."
- **Private / public state** — Stored locally on the user's device, never published / stored on-chain, visible to all.
- **Derived state** — Client-side computation combining public + private state (e.g. `isOwner`).
- **ZKIR** — "Zero-Knowledge Intermediate Representation. A low-level format that Compact smart contracts are compiled into" — the bridge to the ZK backend.
- **Proof server** — "A local service that generates zero-knowledge proofs on behalf of a user's DApp" (Docker, port 6300).
- **Midnight Indexer** — "A component that follows the Midnight chain to index events and data in a queryable database" (GraphQL v4).
- **DApp connector** — "A software interface that allows a DApp … to communicate with a user's Web3 wallet" — `window.midnight.{walletId}`.
- **MidnightProviders** — The six-provider configuration object midnight-js requires: private state, public data, ZK config, proof, wallet, midnight.
- **Contract maintenance authority** — Committee empowered to replace verifier keys/circuits post-deploy; empty committee + threshold 1 = immutable.
- **Contract address** — "A unique identifier assigned to a smart contract when it is deployed" — hash of the deploy part.
- **Domain separator** — Hash-input prefix ensuring a value/signature from one context cannot be reused in another.
- **persistentHash / persistentCommit** — SHA-256-based, upgrade-stable hash/commitment for long-lived state.
- **transientHash / transientCommit** — Circuit-efficient hash/commitment, not guaranteed stable across upgrades.
- **Gadget** — "A specialized entry point, specific to zero-knowledge cryptography, designed to bring ZK Snark circuit development within reach."
- **Bech32m / HRP** — Address encoding with a human-readable prefix identifying type + network (`mn_addr_…`, `mn_shield-addr_…`, `mn_dust_…`).
- **HD wallet** — Hierarchical Deterministic wallet from one master seed; Midnight path `m/44'/2400'/account'/role/index`.
- **Three-wallet model** — WalletFacade coordinating unshielded (NIGHT) + shielded + DUST wallets from one seed.
- **Faucet** — "A web service that distributes free test tokens to developers building on a testnet."
- **Devnet / Testnet / Mainnet** — Development network / intermediate test network (Preview, Preprod) / production chain.
- **Attestation** — Trusted third-party signature over private data (Schnorr on Jubjub), verifiable inside a ZK circuit.
- **Sealed ledger value** — Ledger value unchangeable after constructor execution.
- **NATS** — "A lightweight, high-performance, open-source messaging system" (indexer infrastructure).
- **Federated Node Operators (FNO)** — "A network of independent node operators that work together to maintain and secure the Midnight blockchain."
- **Midnight Expert** — Suite of Claude Code plugins with compiler-verified output for Midnight development.
